assumptions: The constitution and accepted SDD-001 invariants remain authoritative; the draft feature does not implicitly amend them.
Plan statements were considered contextual intent, not substitutes for unresolved behavioral requirements.
This was a read-only specification review. No files were modified, tests executed, tasks created or external systems mutated.
blocking_questions: BQ-01 — Reuse versus mandatory independent re-execution. Constitution §12 and accepted SDD-001 FR-012/AC-014 require outer-runner re-execution; SDD-001 plan explicitly requires every declared verification    command to be re-run after builder PASS. AC-OBS-001 permits skipping execution, while AC-OBS-009 says independent verification remains intact. This determines whether runner reuse is permitted at all.    Smallest decision: explicitly reconcile the accepted policy with reuse, defining which independently produced evidence may satisfy which later invocation and which commands must always execute.

BQ-02 — Required gates and executable decisions. FR-OBS-001/003 do not define how a profile determines mandatory gates or relates to existing task verification commands. The plan says only RUN_NOW executes    but also presents INVALIDATED_BY_THIS_PATCH as a separate classification. A stale mandatory gate could consequently remain invalidated without execution. Smallest decision: define the authoritative required-    gate set, behavior when a task command lacks a profile gate, dependency closure, and whether invalidation is an explanatory reason or an executable state. Define deterministic ordering and blocked-dependent    behavior after failure.

BQ-03 — Fingerprint completeness and scope. FR-OBS-002 leaves result-sensitive inputs to declarations without a minimum completeness contract. AC-OBS-002/003/004 do not settle additions/deletions matching    patterns, dirty or untracked inputs, symlinks, working directory, toolchain/environment changes, sandbox policy, or cache reuse across worktrees. Equal declared hashes can therefore describe materially    different executions. Smallest decision: specify mandatory fingerprint dimensions, file-set semantics, reuse scope, and fail-closed behavior for unknown or non-hermetic inputs; bound 'unrelated edit' to that    declared contract.

BQ-04 — GREEN provenance and tampering threat model. AC-OBS-008 prohibits tampered cache from suppressing execution but does not define who can write cache/evidence or what validates a PASS. A fabricated    record with a matching fingerprint differs from accidental JSON corruption; an editable checksum alone does not establish trusted execution. Smallest decision: define the trusted evidence producer,    adversaries covered, required PASS provenance and integrity checks, and behavior when evidence is missing or unverifiable. Also settle whether corrupt cache automatically triggers fresh execution or blocks    the invocation: the spec promises no manual cleanup, while the plan says invalid cache fails closed.

BQ-05 — Artifact-dependent verification. FM-OBS-006 names overwritten test output but no requirement defines its consequences. A test gate can remain ALREADY_GREEN after its coverage material is deleted or    replaced by a focused run; a dependent coverage command can then consume missing or unrelated output despite unchanged source fingerprints. Smallest decision: define when reuse requires retained output    identity/completeness, what invalidates consumers, and which producer must execute again after material is overwritten. Add an acceptance criterion for this exact counterexample.

BQ-06 — Retry-free critical evidence. INV-OBS-004 is stronger than AC-OBS-007, which prohibits only automatic retry. The spec does not identify critical gates or address command-internal test retries, manual    reinvocation of the same failing fingerprint, and preservation of the initial failure after a later PASS. These choices determine whether failures can be masked. Smallest decision: define critical-gate    designation, prohibited retry layers, permitted recovery after failure, and whether a later successful attempt may satisfy the gate while retaining the earlier failure.

BQ-07 — Concurrent execution, input drift and crash recovery. Atomic writes alone do not specify consistent outcomes across state, events and terminal orchestration evidence. Two direct/runner invocations    can target the same gate, or inputs can change between planning and PASS publication. A crash after command completion but before durable evidence also leaves an uncertain outcome. Smallest decision: define    single-machine ownership and reuse visibility, the rule for inputs changing during execution, and the recoverable outcome at each publication boundary. Require that incomplete or orphaned execution never    becomes reusable GREEN merely because one record says PASS.

BQ-08 — Manual evidence identity and authority. AC-OBS-013/014 leave 'matching full SHA', report/verdict validation and conflicting duplicate undefined. Matching HEAD is not necessarily matching the task    checkpoint or reviewed dirty tree; identical verdicts from different evaluators are not necessarily duplicates. The spec also does not say whether registration affects task completion or only telemetry.    Smallest decision: define required feature/task/attempt/evaluator identity, authoritative checkpoint and clean/dirty-tree rules, report format/hash/verdict binding, idempotency key, exact-repeat behavior,    conflict handling, and whether registration can authorize any workflow transition. Keep independent-evaluator requirements explicit.

BQ-09 — Profile trust and policy changes. Calling a profile trusted repository policy does not establish which revision is authoritative. A builder-controlled worktree could modify gate selection or input    declarations before verification while commands remain allowlisted. Smallest decision: define how accepted profile policy is selected and bound to execution, what happens when it changes during a task, and    whether changes require deliberate re-planning. Direct CLI, runner and orchestrator must apply the same trust rule.

BQ-10 — Telemetry metric semantics and incomplete records. FR-OBS-008 and AC-OBS-011 require factual role/attempt/rework/evaluator metrics without defining counting units, deduplication or missing-data    treatment. Provider invocations, task retries, gate retries and manual evaluator registrations can otherwise be counted as the same kind of attempt. Smallest decision: define these dimensions and aggregation    rules, including abandoned/running records, repeated registration, partial usage/cost and legacy missing fields. Define verification reuse as an observed count; any saved-time or saved-cost figure must be    explicitly estimated with a stated baseline, or omitted.

BQ-11 — Compatibility and rollback behavior. The plan says v1 records remain readable and new fields are optional, but this is not an acceptance contract. It does not settle whether v1 evidence can authorize    reuse, how mixed-version records aggregate, or what an older harness sees after rollback. Smallest decision: specify v1 read/report support, reuse eligibility, unknown-version handling, and rollback/forward-    fix expectations. Distinguish discardable derived cache from failed-attempt and manual-evaluator history that must remain auditable.

BQ-12 — Observable failure and parity contract. The plan promises equivalent plans across entry points, but the spec lacks an AC for parity and does not define failure categories or operator-visible    outcomes. Invalid policy, stale evidence, command failure, unavailable required isolation and evidence-publication failure require different recovery actions. Smallest decision: define stable machine-readable    outcomes and CLI success/failure semantics, actionable diagnostics, and which decision/reason/fingerprint fields must agree across direct CLI, runner and orchestrator for equivalent inputs.

BQ-13 — Secret-minimization boundary. FR-OBS-011 and the plan prohibit secret/prompt contents in telemetry, but environment fingerprints, command arguments, report text and diagnostics can carry them without    copying a raw prompt. Implementations could satisfy the wording while persisting credentials. Smallest decision: define permitted telemetry fields and the handling of sensitive environment values, command    arguments, output excerpts and manual reports, including what is rejected or redacted before persistence. Add a seeded-secret leakage acceptance case.

BQ-14 — Measurable reliability/performance and documentation acceptance. 'Planning should be cheap' provides no testable bound, workload or comparison, and AC-OBS-018 introduces MANUAL TELEMETRY REQUIRED    without defining when it applies or what omission does. Smallest decision: set a representative planning workload and measurable overhead threshold; identify the canonical handbook source/output and define    the manual-registration obligation and omission behavior consistently across executable workflow, READMEs and handbook.

findings: F-01 — Blocking policy conflict: accepted SDD-001 mandates independent outer-runner command re-execution; SDD-OBS-001 does not explicitly authorize or delimit its replacement by cached evidence. See BQ-01.

F-02 — False-GREEN counterexample: unchanged declared source plus changed execution environment can satisfy AC-OBS-001 while producing a different result. Exact fingerprints are insufficient without a    completeness and reuse-scope contract. See BQ-03.

F-03 — Coverage counterexample: full tests PASS, focused tests overwrite reports, then reused full-test GREEN allows coverage over the wrong material. Naming FM-OBS-006 does not define a required rejection    or regeneration outcome. See BQ-05.
F-04 — Retry counterexample: a critical command internally retries a failing test and exits zero. No outer automatic retry occurred, so AC-OBS-007 can pass while INV-OBS-004 is violated. See BQ-06.

F-05 — Crash/concurrency counterexample: state contains PASS but its terminal event is absent, or a command completes after its fingerprinted input changes. Atomic individual writes do not settle whether    either result is reusable. See BQ-07.

F-06 — Manual-evidence counterexample: two reports share SHA and verdict but concern different tasks or evaluators. The existing acceptance criteria cannot distinguish a valid second observation from a    duplicate or conflict. See BQ-08.

F-07 — Compatibility, parity and coverage-ordering assurances occur in plan context or failure-mode lists without sufficient normative acceptance behavior. Existing-suite GREEN alone does not establish these    new contracts.
F-08 — No prototype is justified yet. The identified uncertainties are policy and requirement decisions; empirical experimentation cannot decide their intended semantics.
non_blocking_risks: Conservative invalidation may initially reduce reuse. Once the safety contract is explicit, measured reuse improvements can follow without weakening mandatory verification.
AC-OBS-020 depends on a 'fresh master-agent review'. Reviewer freshness is useful process evidence, but repeatable fixtures must carry the deterministic acceptance claims.
The no-remote-authority boundary is clearly retained by INV-OBS-008 and AC-OBS-019. Regression evidence should cover all new entry points without introducing a new remote workflow.
residual_risks: Implementation correctness, architecture suitability and runtime behavior were not assessed.
The tamper-resistance guarantee cannot be evaluated until the accepted threat model distinguishes accidental corruption, untrusted provider writes and a hostile local actor.
After requirements are resolved, the architecture grill and independently authored verification contract remain required before executable task generation.
summary: The spec is not ready for task generation. It identifies the relevant failure classes but leaves contract-affecting decisions unresolved, including a conflict with accepted mandatory outer-runner    re-execution. The blockers below concern requirements and observable behavior only; the technical plan was read as context, not architecture-grilled.
